draftText: Our clinic has 12 doctors and about 200 patient visits per day. Reception fills the appointment book in Google Sheets and patients often come at the wrong time or not at all (~15% no-shows). We would like a reminder system.

fields.title: Appointment reminders with confirmation and slot release
fields.context: The clinic has 12 doctors and about 200 patient visits per day. Reception keeps the appointment book in Google Sheets. Around 15% of patients do not show up or come at the wrong time, so doctors have idle slots.
fields.need: Automatically remind patients a day before the visit, let them confirm or cancel, and free the slot when they cancel.
fields.users: Reception staff (3 people) and patients who receive the messages
fields.data: Appointment book in Google Sheets (columns: date, time, doctor, phone); export of the last 6 months with names removed; no-show statistics per doctor
fields.constraints: Patient names must not leave the clinic server — only phone numbers and times may go to the messaging provider; deadline 8 weeks; WhatsApp or SMS
fields.expectedResult: A service that reads the appointment sheet, sends WhatsApp/SMS reminders 24 hours before, records confirm/cancel replies and marks freed slots in the sheet.
fields.successCriteria: No-show rate drops from 15% to under 8% within a month of the pilot; 90% of reminders delivered; freed slots visible to reception within 5 minutes.
fields.contact: Clinic administrator, weekly 30-minute call on Tuesdays, questions in a shared Telegram chat within one business day

techSpec.summary: Reminder service for a clinic: reads appointments from Google Sheets, sends WhatsApp/SMS reminders 24 h before the visit, processes confirm/cancel replies and frees cancelled slots. Suggested stack is a recommendation.
scope: Sync appointments from Google Sheets every 15 minutes
Send reminder 24 h before the visit
Mark cancelled slots as free in the sheet
dataInputs: Google Sheet: date, time, doctor, phone
functionalRequirements: Only phone number, date and time are sent to the messaging provider
Retry failed messages up to 3 times
Reception can trigger a manual reminder
Reply keywords work in Kazakh and Russian
nonFunctional: Runs on the clinic's own server (Docker)
acceptanceCriteria: No-show rate under 8% in the pilot month
Freed slot appears in the sheet within 5 minutes
suggestedStack: WhatsApp Business API or SMS gateway
openQuestions: Which messaging provider does the clinic already have a contract with?
Should reminders also go to the doctor?

draftText: We have 3 grocery stores in Almaty. Every evening the store managers count leftovers by hand and send photos to WhatsApp; the buyer then decides what to order tomorrow.

fields.title: Evening stock count and next-day order suggestion for 3 stores
fields.context: Three grocery stores in Almaty. Every evening store managers count leftovers by hand and send photos to a WhatsApp group; the buyer decides tomorrow's order from the photos.
fields.need: Collect evening counts in a structured form and suggest an order per store so the buyer stops reading photos.
fields.data: Daily sales export from the 1C cashier system (CSV, 12 months, ~400 SKUs); supplier price list in Excel
fields.constraints: Managers use Android phones; the tool must work in a browser; first version in 6 weeks
fields.expectedResult: A mobile-friendly web form for the evening count and a page that shows the suggested order for each store based on sales history.
fields.successCriteria: Buyer spends under 20 minutes per evening on ordering (now ~60); stock-outs of top-50 SKUs reduced by 30%.

techSpec.summary: Web tool for three grocery stores: structured evening stock count and a next-day order suggestion computed from 12 months of 1C sales data. Suggested stack is a recommendation.
scope: Order suggestion per SKU per store
Buyer review page with editable quantities
functionalRequirements: Suggestion = expected sales for next day minus current stock, rounded to pack size
Export the approved order to Excel
acceptanceCriteria: Buyer time under 20 minutes per evening
Stock-outs of top-50 SKUs reduced by 30% over a month
openQuestions: Who is the contact person and how often can the team ask questions?
Is there a pack-size field in the price list?

draftText: Dispatchers call drivers every morning to tell them the route. We want a simple app for routes.

fields.title: Morning route sheet for drivers
fields.context: Dispatchers call each of the 25 drivers every morning to dictate the route; calls take about an hour.
fields.need: Send each driver the day's route automatically instead of calling.
fields.data: Route table in Excel updated the evening before (driver, stops, addresses)
fields.expectedResult: A Telegram bot or web page where each driver sees their route for the day.
fields.contact: Head of dispatch, questions by phone or Telegram

techSpec.summary: Daily route delivery to drivers from an Excel route table, via Telegram bot or a mobile web page. Suggested stack is a recommendation.
scope: Send route to each driver at 07:00
dataInputs: Excel route table: driver, stops, addresses
functionalRequirements: One message per driver with ordered stops
Dispatcher can re-send after a change
openQuestions: What are the deadline and technology constraints?

draftText: Parents keep calling to ask about schedule changes and homework. Need some kind of bot. ASAP.

fields.title: Parent bot for schedule and homework
fields.context: Parents call the school office several times a day to ask about schedule changes and homework.
fields.need: Give parents a bot that answers schedule and homework questions so the office gets fewer calls.

draftText: We make custom kitchens. Improve efficiency of our production planning, etc. We have some data in Excel.

fields.title: Production planning board for a custom kitchen workshop
fields.context: A workshop of 14 people makes custom kitchens; orders are planned in one shared Excel file that the foreman updates by hand, so the sales team never knows when an order will be ready.
fields.need: Show the sales team and the foreman one live view of which orders are in which stage and when they are due.
fields.data: Planning Excel with orders, stages (cutting, edging, assembly, delivery) and dates for 2025–2026; photos of the whiteboard used on the floor
fields.constraints: No budget for paid software; must run on the workshop's Windows PC; first version in 5 weeks
fields.expectedResult: A web dashboard with a board of orders by stage, due dates and an overdue list, fed from the Excel file.
fields.successCriteria: Sales can answer 'when is my order ready' without calling the foreman; late deliveries fall from 25% to 10%.
fields.contact: Workshop owner, weekly visit or call, Telegram for quick questions

techSpec.summary: Kanban-style production dashboard for a furniture workshop, reading orders and stages from the existing planning Excel file. Suggested stack is a recommendation.
dataInputs: Planning Excel: order, client code, stages, dates
functionalRequirements: Changes on the board write back to the Excel or a small database
acceptanceCriteria: Sales answers readiness questions without calling
openQuestions: Does the foreman have a PC or tablet on the floor?
